entry.purpose: Canonical JSON bytes: sorted keys, tight separators, ensure_ascii=False — the one serialization every hash and seal in this module is computed over (the pmca_pools and pmca_write_in_storage precedents).
Canonical JSON of an object as text.
Host-asserted timestamp: a hash input only, never evidence (the pools precedent).
Words for an index (the pmca_pools _extract_words pattern): a 'words' list if present, else lowercase alphanumeric tokens from every string in the structure.
The per-run step fold recorded as an incomplete entry's journal_head_hash: GENESIS folded over the steps in order. Recomputable from a filed entry's steps alone.

Entry_v 1 environment discipline (spec 4.5): every key always present, and the dictionary block ALWAYS named — configured or explicitly off. A record that names no dictionary is malformed and is refused here, at write time, not discovered at check time.
A state block with every key always present, null when unused, never absent (spec 4.2/4.5). Unknown keys are refused; missing keys are filled with null.

Parse a JSONL chain file. Returns (records, truncated, good_end): a torn FINAL line is truncation (the pools _load_file precedent) and is dropped; a bad line anywhere else, or a non-object line, raises loudly. A missing file parses as an empty chain.
Candidate gap keys inside a step's data: values of gap-naming fields, and any string carrying the '::' gap-key shape (the section 2.2 gaps-index key form).
True when any nested dict carries a 'graph' field equal to the target address (stored as a JSON list, the pools graph-field precedent).
Build the incomplete-process store's word index over the filed records.
Index one incomplete record under every word its input contains.
Module-internal: EntryStore extends the view when it files. Not a door; never called by readers.
The incomplete entry filed for one process id, or None.
Incomplete entries whose recorded input mentions the word, in seq order.
Incomplete entries carrying the status. INCOMPLETE is the only status this pack writes; the door exists so any future status is searchable the day it exists.
Incomplete entries by provenance: which process family died.

Incomplete entries whose steps contain a recorded gap for the word/identifier — findable from the gap the process died on. The identifier may be a full gap key (matched exactly) or a key component (matched against the key's '::' parts alongside the word).
Incomplete entries whose recorded input or steps carry the graph address (a (layer, dimension, index) triple, stored as a JSON list).
Initialise a handle for one in-flight process: its store, entry id and unsealed state.
True once this handle's process has sealed its entry.
Journal one step of this process, fsynced before returning.

Seal the process into the main entry store and return the sealed entry. Falls back to the outcome / ending_state attributes the caller set on the handle. starting_state, when given, supersedes the journal's begun-state record FOR THE SEALED ENTRY ONLY (the journal's entry_open keeps the begun state): the analyzer's entry builder resolves segment membership at seal time and stamps the sealed entry with it, while state_before_checksum rides through from the begin (see pmca_sentence_analyzer._seal_analysis_entry).
Initialise a closed, empty entry store; files and locks are taken by open.

Open the entry store rooted at <root>/atomic/ and return the store. Exclusive open returns with .recoveries holding the incomplete entries this open filed (possibly empty) — surfaced, never silent. Raises EntryStoreLocked when a live writer holds the store; ArchiveLocked when a seal_v 2 entry names a key the configured keyring cannot supply.
Release the entry store's writer flock and close its descriptor.

Close append handles and release the lock file. In-flight journal runs are NOT sealed or filed by closing: in the journal they are indistinguishable from a hard death, and the next exclusive open files them (spec 4.6 trigger 2). Idempotent.
The path of a named file inside the entry store directory.
Load the main, journal and incomplete files, truncating torn final lines when writable and indexing what was read.
Verify the main file's chain: entry version, sequence and previous-seal linkage, raising on any corruption.
Verify the incomplete file's chain: version, sequence, ids and previous-seal linkage, raising on any corruption.
Verify the journal file's chain: sequence, previous-hash linkage and record hashes, raising on any corruption.
Rebuild the in-flight process runs from the journal records.
Re-verify all three chains against the in-memory state. True, or raise ValueError (the pools verify_chain idiom).
The canonical bytes an entry's seal covers: the entry minus its seal fields.
Seal a new entry: HMAC under the domain subkey when a write key is configured (seal_v 2), else the unkeyed SHA-256 form (seal_v 1).
Verify an entry's seal against its material and the configured keyring, raising when it cannot be verified.
Open append handles for the main, journal and incomplete files, creating them when absent.
Write one line to a store file and fsync before acknowledgement.
Raise when the entry store is closed or was opened read-only.
Index one sealed entry under every word its input, outcome and steps contain.
The seal append: one canonical line, write+fsync, then the in-memory append — one critical section under the store lock (spec 6.1).
Append one hash-chained record to the process journal under the store lock.
Begin a wrapped process (spec 4.4 step 1): allocate the entry_id and append the journal entry_open record, fsynced BEFORE the process runs. From this moment the process's existence is durable.
Append one step record for an in-flight process, refusing sealed or finished processes.
Seal an in-flight process into the main file as one entry carrying its input, steps and outcome.

Wrap a process in the entry lifecycle (spec 4.4). On clean exit the handle's outcome is sealed (an explicit handle.seal() inside the block takes precedence). On ANY exception — including a failing seal append — the process is filed incomplete immediately and the original exception re-raised unchanged (spec 4.6 trigger 1). Acknowledgement of an outcome happens only after its entry is durable.

File one unterminated journal run incomplete, or retire it without filing when its entry already sealed in the main store (idempotent by entry_id — spec 4.4 step 3). Returns the filed incomplete entry, or None when the run needed no filing.
Open recovery (spec 4.6 trigger 2): holding the lock file is proof no live writer owns the store, so every unterminated journal run is dead. File each and return the filings.
Explicit sweep (spec 4.6): re-run the recovery scan under this store's exclusivity. Idempotent by entry_id; returns the entries filed by THIS call.
Append a segment lifecycle entry (open, close or discard) to the main file.

A segment_open entry: carries opening_fingerprint and the starting_state_blob — the serialized starting state INSIDE the entry (spec 4.2), written by the same append that opens the segment. There is no code path that opens a segment without it.

A segment_close entry carrying the close fields exactly as the existing segment_close payload computes them (reason, engagements, first_seq, last_seq, segment_head, closing_fingerprint, key), so the key discipline is continuous with existing chains. first_seq/last_seq refer to entry seqs in this store.
A segment_discard entry: a discarded segment is marked by a record, never vaporized.
Entry by main-store seq, or None.
Sealed entries whose input, outcome, or steps mention the word, in seq order.
All sealed entries in seq order. Deterministic.
The atomic-entries battery assertion helper: record and print PASS or FAIL for a named condition.
The fixed environment record the atomic-entries battery seals its test entries under.
A file's bytes, or empty bytes when the file does not exist.
The atomic-entries module's own test battery, run over a temporary store root.
The atomic-entries battery body: append, chain, journal, incomplete-filing and lock cases over the given root.
The tree's one serialization: sorted keys, tight separators (pmca_atomic_entries._canonical precedent).
Canonical bytes of an object, for hashing and seals.
SHA-256 of a file's bytes (the code_hash source).
Deterministic gap id (spec section 4.4, F-9): first 16 hex of SHA-256 of the canonical {kind, target_id, code_hash}; code_hash is null for store-level kinds.
True for a module's own check/main harness functions, which carry the self_check surface (spec section 4.2 rule 4 + the F-12 deviation rule in this module's MANIFEST comment).
The pinned surfaces_served for one scoped function: the module default from the MANIFEST, or ["self_check"] for harness functions.
Parse one hash-chained JSONL store file. Returns (records, truncated). A torn final line is truncation; corruption anywhere else, a broken chain, or a bad seal raises RegistryError naming the file.
Initialise a closed store handle for a directory; files are verified and the lock taken by open.
Open (creating if needed) the store at directory, verify both chains, and take the single-writer lock unless read_only. Returns the open store.
Release the writer lock and close the store.
Raise RegistryLocked when the store is not open for writing under this handle.
Append one sealed, hash-chained record: allocate seq and seal in the same critical section as the write, fsync before acknowledgement.
Append one entry version, allocating its seq and chain seal in the same critical section as the write. Returns the sealed record.
Append one gap record to the gaps file. Returns the sealed record.
Append a gap-closure record (the only way a gap closes; gap records are never edited or deleted).
id -> standing version record. The standing version is the highest-seq version; a standing version marked retracted means the id has NO standing entry (F-4: retraction is a state, not prose).
(open_gaps, closed_ids): gap records keyed by gap id, minus those closed by a later closure record.

Load a registry store read-only (no lock, no writes): verify both chains and rebuild every index in memory. Returns a dict with standing entries, all versions, and gap state. The files are the record; the indexes are doors, rebuilt — never a second stored copy.
The standing entry dict for entry_id in a loaded registry, or None.
The alphanumeric/underscore tokens of a text, lowercased — the exact-token unit of purpose and limit search.
Standing entries matching a predicate, in id order.
Exact search by entry id; empty list when absent — never a near match.
Exact search by qualname, or by bare function name across modules.
Exact token match over purpose text.
Exact search by parameter name or annotation string.
Exact search by returns-annotation string.
Exact token match over limits and hold_conditions.
Exact search by generation value; None returns the null / generation-gap population.
Exact search by surface (closed vocabulary).
Search by EFFECTIVE status (derived, spec section 1.2): gap-flagged iff an open gap references the id.
Search gap records by kind, by referenced entry id, and by open/closed state.

The scoped function set, by the spec section 4.2 AST rule over the MANIFEST modules: module-level functions plus methods directly in a class body, in file order; dunders excluded except __init__; nested functions and nested-class functions excluded. Recomputed from the current files at every call — never cached.
Field-shape problems of a standing entry (the missing_field check): a required field absent or of the wrong type. Returns a list of problem strings.

Registrar act: validate and append one entry version. A re-registration of the same id is a supersession (the new version's supersedes names the standing version's seq), never a second entry. Returns the sealed record.

Retraction as a STATE (F-4): append a superseding version of the standing entry with status "retracted" and retracted True, its purpose recording the retraction. There is no delete. After retraction the id has no standing entry, so Direction 1 reports it uncovered.

Adapter for WG3's registration hook (F-3): WG4 calls SelfFixLoop.registration_hook with a callable; this callable receives capability_description() as data and files it as registrar provenance material for the loop's per-function entries. The description gets NO entry under its own id (pmca.self_fix_loop names no code locus and would be a phantom by construction). Returns the description filed.
Purpose text from a function's own docstring: its first paragraph, whitespace-flattened (quoted source, provenance purpose_source "docstring").

Author one registry entry for one enumerated function (the registrar path): purpose from the docstring when one exists, else from registrar_purposes (purpose_source "registrar" — a purpose is never invented silently; a function with neither is refused loudly here so the bootstrap cannot pass it over). Signature and annotations are read from the live code object by inspect — a description of the locus, never a call.
The pinned id of the standing generation gap (F-9): derived from {kind, target, code_hash null} exactly as _gap_id derives every gap id.

Bootstrap seeding, in the spec section 4.5 order: (1) create the store; (2) register every manifest entry (the amended manifest, including this module's own); (3) append the generation gap; (4) return a summary. The self pointer (step 5) is written by the caller's stored-once amendment path; the first checker run (step 6) is the caller's next act. Refuses to bootstrap over a non-empty store.

Direction 2 resolution in a subprocess (the teaching verification-subprocess precedent): import each module and walk the qualname by attribute. Attributes are resolved only — no scoped function is ever called.

The completeness check, store-vs-code in both directions plus the self-pointer detector (F-5). Appends gap records and gap closures to the gaps file only; never registers, supersedes, or edits an entry. Returns the check report dict (with exit_code 0/1; a store that cannot be read raises RegistryError, which run_checks maps to exit 2).
Run the checker and return its report; a checker that cannot complete (store unreadable / corrupt) returns a report with exit_code 2 instead of raising.
Runner: python3 pmca_capability_registry.py [registry_root] [tree_root]. Prints the check report as canonical JSON and exits with its exit code (0/1/2).

Total a sentence's harm pairs through the cascade and return the totaling verdict: HOLD no_edges_no_event on empty harms (B-2, ruled 2026-10-30), REFUSE on intrinsic harm, and the gate comparison on the total otherwise, exactly as the calculus states.
Point the module at a genus store file (mirrors the analyzer's configure_dictionary pattern).

The id of the genus a form names, or None when no genus matches.
The stored referral for a word, or None. Reads every genus entry's members; a word has an is_a only where a referral is stored — nothing is inferred.

The word's own differentia: its first stored dictionary definition, read at answer time from the dictionary tier (its own stored fact, quoted — never copied into the genus entry). Returns (text, provenance) or (None, None).

The referral's distinct provenance lineage CLASSES, read through the governed source->lineage table (Candidacy Rule Set C-3; pmca_lineage_table): spelling variants of one lineage are ONE class (Ledger D-2, fixed 2026-11-01), and a provenance record with a missing/empty lineage (and no usable source) counts as NO class, never as a class (Ledger D-3, fixed 2026-11-01; pre-fix, a missing lineage counted as the None class, so [{}, {lineage: Webster}] honoured a VERIFIED referral on one real lineage).

Find the noun an adjective attaches to: next NOUN in [lo, hi), skipping ADJ/DET. Returns noun index or None.

Tier 1 simple parse (no relative clauses). Returns Parse or None.

Tier 2 fallback: Longest-Match + Dependency Adjacency. Content tokens form a flat sequential dependency chain. Less precise than Tier 1, but explicit and deterministic. Returns Parse or None.
Full Layer 1 pipeline: tokenize -> idiom -> compound -> POS -> Tier 1 -> Tier 2 -> HOLD. Never guesses; HOLD on any unresolvable input.

The entries a parse produced: one per distinct token surface, in first-appearance order. Pure function of the Parse; the entry payloads are plain data (dicts/lists/strings/ints/None).

Place the entries a parse produced into a working GraphSpace: Layer 1 graphs chosen by dist_address, produced on demand (created_by "system"). A caller may pass a shared space, in which case graphspace glue rules apply: re-placing a word with a differing entry raises GlueConflict. Returns the space.
The working GraphSpace materialized by the most recent parse() call (a fresh space per call), or None before any parse.
Parse text and place the produced entries into a fresh working GraphSpace. Returns (Parse, GraphSpace).

Parse text (see _parse_pipeline) and place the produced entries into a fresh working GraphSpace (see place_parse). The Parse result is exactly the pipeline's result; placement is additional addressing only and never alters a parse output.
Convert a Layer 1 Parse to a pmca_proof.ParseResult so the Layer 2 gate (build_edges + gate_verdict) can consume it.

Layer 1 parse -> Layer 2 gate, multi-clause. Every clause is parsed and its edges collected; ALL edges from ALL clauses feed one gate verdict (same combine rule as pmca_proof.evaluate: noisy-OR over all edges; any held clause lifts APPROVE/REDACT to HOLD). Returns (verdict, parses) where parses is one Parse per clause.
AST check: no call to maximum anywhere in this file.
AST check: no float literal anywhere in this file.
AST check: no random import anywhere in this file.
Grep check: the forbidden guessing verb does not appear in this file. Pattern is built from parts so the checker does not match itself.
The layer-1 parser's own test battery.
The canonical form of a spelling, under the stated deterministic rule: case-fold, then delete every character that is not a letter or a digit.
Build the canonical-form to lineage map from the governed source table, raising on a canonical collision between spellings of different lineages.

Append one ungoverned-source gap record for `spelling` (as written) resolved in `context` to the gap store, under the ATOM-2 single-writer lock for the gap file's directory. Returns the record written, or None when this (spelling, context) was already logged in this process. A lock that stays held past the retry budget raises (pmca_persistence.WriterLockHeld): the append never happens unlocked, and the failure is loud, never a silent gap about a gap.

Resolve one source/lineage spelling to its governed lineage class, or None when the spelling carries NO class (missing, None, non-string, empty/whitespace). Resolution is by canonical form (see the module docstring): any case/space/punctuation variant of a governed spelling resolves to that spelling's lineage. A spelling whose canonical form is ungoverned resolves to itself AS WRITTEN (self-identity, never merged) and is recorded as an ungoverned-source gap in `context`.
The lineage class of one provenance record, or None (NO class). "lineage" governs when present and non-empty; else "source"; else no class. Non-dict records carry no key and contribute no class.

The set of lineage classes over provenance records; records with NO class contribute nothing. `context` names the counter doing the resolving and is carried into any ungoverned-source gap record produced.
The exact-headword entry for a word, or None. pmca_dictionary.lookup resolves suffix variants itself; the entry counts as exact only when the headword it reports IS the word asked for.

A definition with its leading GCIDE apparatus stripped: "(Zoöl.)" field labels and "(a)" sense markers are apparatus, not sense text. The ONE shared implementation (pmca_verb_capable.clean_sense_text, Candidacy Rule Set; WG2 2026-11-01 — this module's CLEANED copy is RETIRED as a mechanism and survives only as this delegation).
GCIDE convention: a verb sense is a definition beginning "To ", read after apparatus labels — the one shared decoding (pmca_verb_capable.is_verb_sense, CANDIDATE evidence under C-4).
(has_verb_senses, has_nonverb_senses) over stored defs.
If the entry is a pure cross-reference stub (a single short definition whose content is "See {X}"), return X lowercased; else None.

Rule-generated candidate bases: {base: {forms}}. Generation only — nothing here is accepted until the base attests as an exact headword. -s endings yield both the plural and third_person readings of the same base.

Stored definition d is covered by another entry's definition o: equal, or contained either way with the contained text substantial (>= 30 chars) — short fragments shared across entries are not coverage.

For the stub check: the sorted names of OTHER entries whose stored definitions, taken together, contain every one of the token's definitions (verbatim or by containment). Bounded fragment search over the same DB file, read-only. Returns None when the check cannot run (tier off).
Assemble a morphology resolution result record for a token.
A HOLD morphology result for a token with the given reason and evidence.
Resolve one token to its entry and form. See the module docstring for the evidence discipline.
Accept the single rule-generated base. The -s family is two-way: the standalone reading follows the base entry's attested senses.

All attested (entry, form) readings of a token, for agreement: the resolve_form result when it resolves, plus BOTH -s readings when a base attests (the verb slot reads the third_person shape; the plural is its noun reading).
Person/number agreement between a subject and a verb token. See the module docstring.
Resolve each word once and group by entry. Returns plain data: {"families": {entry: {form: token}}, "held": [{"word", "hold_reason"}], "counts": {...}}.
The morphology finder's own agreement battery, run against the stored Webster 1913 dictionary.

Default oracle: the word has a noun subcoordinate in the stored dictionary. The ONE shared implementation (pmca_verb_capable.noun_capable, Candidacy Rule Set C-4; WG2 2026-11-01 — this copy's former RAW "To " test is RETIRED as a mechanism, DICT-1 Part 1).

Default oracle: the word has a verb subcoordinate in the stored dictionary. The ONE shared implementation (pmca_verb_capable.verb_capable, Candidacy Rule Set C-4; WG2 2026-11-01 — this copy's former RAW "To " test is RETIRED as a mechanism, DICT-1 Part 1).

The first definition's opening text, with one leading parenthesized field label ("(Zoöl.)" and kin) stripped, or None when the word has no entry. (The adjective microscript's measurement primitive, hoisted in Pack A.)

Measured entry evidence for an adjective use: an entry exists whose first definition opens as a quality, not as a genus phrase and not as a verb form. This is the adjective microscript's adjective_capable rule (measured 13/14 adjectives, 8/10 nouns on its labeled sample; the mass nouns "stone" and "meat" are its named false positives), stated once here so every surface judges a modifier by the same evidence.

Determined-or-ambiguous adverb evidence for the slot guards: the word's morphology attestation is adverbial_ly (its use as an adverb is DETERMINED), or it is a member of the closed unmarked-adverb lexeme list (its adverb use is attested by the grammar list while its noun use is attested by the dictionary — an ambiguous token). Either way the word cannot be taken as a noun-phrase head; see adverb_slot_check for how the two cases differ.
Only the determined case: morphology attests the word's form as adverbial_ly.

A following token that makes a contraction's expansion ambiguous (is vs has): an attested verb form spelled as a participle — regular (-ed / -en, entry form "verb") or a member of the closed irregular-participle list (Pack A; Argon F4: gone / hurt / cut / run carry no suffix signal). The list is itself the participle attestation (a closed grammar list, like CONTRACTIONS): this dictionary build stores some of these words' verb senses without a "To " opening ("cut" resolves with form "other"), so a verb-capability gate would silently exempt exactly the words the list exists for; a stored entry is required.

Xs' stem verification: the full form is an attested plural noun — it resolves as a plural form through morphology, or it is itself a stored noun headword (the wolves case), and it is noun-capable in the dictionary.

The head noun after a possessive clitic: the phrase head is the LAST noun-capable token of the noun-phrase span that follows the clitic — the span runs to the first verb-capable token, article, preposition, splitter, auxiliary, pronoun, or further clitic. Leading tokens that are neither noun- nor verb-capable are skipped (the adjective-slot tokens of the original rule); once a noun-capable token is seen, a token that is neither ends the span. Return (head, index) or (None, None).
Genitive + contraction normalization of a token list.
Indices of attested finite-verb tokens: verb-capable and not an auxiliary/modal grammar token.
Split token indices into segments at splitter tokens.

Finite verbs as Guard 2 counts them: attested finite-verb tokens minus tokens in determined noun position (immediately preceded by an article, or a genitive phrase head immediately preceded by its possessor stem) and minus possessor stems themselves.
Guards 2 and 4 over a token list. Returns a HOLD tag or None.

The phrase-head candidate of a span under the finder template (the head is the phrase's last nominal token): the rightmost noun-capable token, skipping articles and possessor stems. Returns (token, index) or (None, None).

The index-span truncated at its first preposition token: the noun phrase proper. A prepositional phrase inside a subject or object span ("the wolf of the forest", "eats with the wolf") belongs to the preposition layer; the slot guards judge only the NP before it.

Yield (segment_indices, verb_index) for each segment (splitter-delimited run) whose verb geometry is determined for the slot guards: exactly one counted finite verb — or exactly two ADJACENT counted verbs where the first is noun-capable and a non-empty object span follows the second (the first is then a noun-phrase-internal token, as in "the wolf pack hunts the sheep": the counted-verb list sees "pack", the phrase parse sees a subject NP ending in "pack" and the verb "hunts"). Segments of any other shape are owned by the other guards and the consumers' ambiguity machinery (e.g. "The sheep hunt duck." keeps its ambiguous_verb_candidates HOLD: there the second verb has no object span, and two full parses compete).
Guard 6 (Pack A; claims-03 W1/W2/W5, claims-07 2.1): an adverb-attested token as a noun-phrase head. Returns a HOLD tag or None.
Guard 7 (Pack A; claims-07 2.2, divergence D22): a modifier whose adjective use is not attested. Returns a HOLD tag or None.
Guards 5, 2, 4 over a normalized token list, in binding order (Guard 3 is surface-specific: passive_signature below; Guard 1 lives in the consumers' ambiguity machinery). Returns a HOLD tag or None.
Guard 3 geometry: an AUX_BE token immediately followed by a verb-form token, or an AUX_BE token with a later "by" phrase. Returns True when the passive signature is present.

The finder microscripts' grammar-word lock: a modal, a do-auxiliary, or negation anywhere in the sentence HOLDs with the scope tag — those words' uses are grammatical, and v1 scope cannot place them, so they must never be read as content. Returns the scope tag or None.

ST-20 guard (2026-10-27): "not" inside a clause's target span, before the noun-phrase head, negates the target itself. The analyzer's head scan breaks a span at "not" — correct for the verb group in a SUBJECT span ("The wolf does not eat ...") — but in a TARGET span the break drops the target with no candidate seen, and before this guard the clause was skipped silently and the sentence approved below the gate ("He deliberately poisons not the child." -> APPROVE (0, 1); the control REFUSEs). Negation geometry is out of v1 scope exactly as it is for "never" (negation_out_of_scope:never); the grammar lock above covers the finder surfaces sentence-wide, but it does not run on the analyzer surface (the analyzer parses the verb group itself), so this guard covers the one position the lock cannot see: the span after the clause's verb. The scan mirrors the head scan's: a preposition before any head candidate does not end the span (its object may still be the head), one after the head does; an auxiliary ends it (a following verb group is not this clause's target). "not" AFTER the head is a contrastive tail ("breaks the cup not the window") — the head was bound and evaluated, not dropped — and returns None. Returns the HOLD tag or None.

The full shared screen, in binding order: genitive normalization first (tokenization layer), then Guard 5, the grammar lock, Guard 2, Guard 4, and (Pack A) the adverb slot guard and the noun-adjunct guard. Returns the normalize() dict plus "hold" possibly set by a later guard (on a guard HOLD, tokens/genitives from normalization are preserved for the caller's record but MUST NOT be bound from).

The adverb lock on an OK finder result: if the bound target is the sentence-final token and its morphology attestation is adverbial_ly, its use in this sequence is adverb — rebuild the result with target None and the token relabeled as an adverb use. Shared by every finder surface (their result dicts share the sentence/verdict/hold_reason/ uses/subject/verb/target core). Returns the result, corrected in a copy; non-OK results pass through.

Possessor labeling on an OK primary-finder result: a possessor stem the phrase template labeled "adjective" is relabeled to its determined use — noun, subcoordinate "possessor" — and the result gains a "possessors" list of {"head", "possessor"} records. Returns the result, corrected in a copy.
Read and validate the config file at path.
Encode a state value into JSON-safe typed form.
Reverse encode_typed. Raises PersistenceError on bad tags.
Fsync a directory so a rename inside it is durable. (A file fsync alone does not persist the directory entry; claims audit 09, Claim 4.)
Write data (bytes) to path atomically.
Acquire the single-writer lock for a storage root.
Release a writer lock acquired by acquire_lock.
Canonical JSON text: sorted keys, fixed separators.
Canonical JSON bytes of a persistence envelope.
Read and parse a save file's envelope, raising PersistenceError naming the path when it is unreadable, not valid JSON, or not an object.
Validate a save envelope's kind and format against what the loader wants, raising on a kind mismatch or an unsupported format.
Run a save's read-back load (Pack H save/load symmetry).
The domain-separated state-seal subkey for one key id and artifact kind ("seed_dict" or "analyzer_space").

Load a keyring and return (key_id, master key bytes) for state sealing: the named key, or the ring's current key. ArchiveLocked if the keyring or the named key is absent (the module's existing vocabulary for an absent key).
The sealed material of a seed save: canonical_seed_json(seed) (pending keys and metadata included) plus the canonical JSON of the teaching block.

The LEGACY (pre-Pack-H, seal_v absent) seed seal: unkeyed SHA-256 over the sealed material, the envelope generation outside it. Kept so pre-Pack-H files verify for adoption; new saves never write this form.
seal_v 1: unkeyed SHA-256 over the sealed material with the envelope generation inside it.
seal_v 2: HMAC-SHA256 under the seed state subkey over the sealed material with the envelope generation inside it.
Persist the current seed dict plus teaching's counter and audit log to <root>/seed_state.json. Returns the file path.

Load and fully verify a seed save. Returns (envelope, seed, teaching_block). Nothing is returned unless the module seal verifies, the decoded state re-materializes, and (for a non-pending seed) pmca_seed.verify() passes. The returned envelope carries "seal_state": "adopted_unsealed" (a pre-Pack-H file, verified under its legacy digest), "unkeyed" (seal_v 1), or "keyed" (seal_v 2). A seal_v 2 file REQUIRES keyring_path: without it, or without the envelope's named key, ArchiveLocked is raised — never a silent unverified load.
Load the persisted seed dict. Returns (seed, teaching_block).

True iff an entry is a graphspace glue marker: a dict whose only key is "glued", holding a 3-part address. (That shape is reserved by the format; a canonical entry of exactly that shape cannot be distinguished from a marker and is refused at save.)
The persisted structure of a GraphSpace: every graph in sorted address order, with its meta, its edges, and its entries EXCLUDING analysis records (Decision 4: records are scratch, never persisted).

Rebuild a GraphSpace from a persisted structure, through the guarded graphspace calls only: produce_graph per graph, canonical entries via place_entry first across all graphs, glue markers second (each checked against the rebuilt address book), then edges via place_edge in order. Any guard failure raises PersistenceError; the half-built space is a local and is never returned.

The record-filtered checksum of an analyzer own space: the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of a throwaway space materialized from the space's persisted structure (typed encode/decode round trip, analysis records excluded per Decision 4, exactly the round trip a load performs). This is the checksum save_analyzer_space seals a save with, factored out so callers (the falsifiability engagement records) can fingerprint a space without saving it.
Persist an analyzer own space to <root>/analyzer_space.json. Returns the file path.

Load and fully verify an analyzer space save. Returns (envelope, space). The space is materialized through the guarded calls and its canonical bytes must verify against the saved checksum, else SealMismatch and the space is discarded (never returned). The returned envelope carries "seal_state": "adopted_unsealed" (a pre-Pack-H file: checksum is the bare SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, generation outside), "unkeyed" (seal_v 1: generation inside), or "keyed" (seal_v 2: HMAC, generation inside). A seal_v 2 file REQUIRES keyring_path: without it, or without the envelope's named key, ArchiveLocked is raised.
Load the persisted analyzer own space. Returns a GraphSpace.
Boot-restore from the config at config_path.
Release the writer lock held by a boot() report.
Numeric part of a keyring key id ("k12" -> 12).

Domain-separated subkeys for one key id: HMAC-SHA256 over the domain label, the key id as u32be, and the archive format major as u16be. The master key is never used directly, so the encryption key and the authentication key are independent, and a future format version derives fresh subkeys automatically.
HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream: block i is HMAC-SHA256(enc_key, nonce_material || i as u64be), i from 0, truncated to nbytes.
Byte-wise XOR of data with a pad.
True iff a float occurs anywhere inside obj.
Write a keyring file atomically: temp file in the same directory (mkstemp, so the file is created mode 0600 and key material is never world-readable), flush, fsync, rename.
Create a new keyring at path with one key, "k1", and return the keyring dict. Refuses, loudly, to overwrite an existing keyring: overwriting would orphan every entry the old keys protect.
Load and validate a keyring file. Missing file -> ArchiveLocked. Malformed content -> PersistenceError.

Append a fresh key to an existing keyring, make it current, and return the new key id ("k2", "k3", ...). Old keys are never removed: a key that protects any existing entry must stay readable forever -- rotation adds keys, it never retires the ability to read.
The authenticated header of an archive entry: every field except the ciphertext and the tag, as canonical JSON bytes.
Encrypt one archive entry and return its entry dict: {"v", "seq", "key_id", "label", "nonce", "ct", "tag"}.
Decrypt one archive entry against a loaded keyring dict and return its payload.
The archive file's path under a root.
The next append sequence: the current line count of the archive file (0 if absent). The archive is append-only, so this is strictly increasing for the life of the archive.
The archive head file's path under a root.
Domain-separated subkey for the archive head chain: HMAC-SHA256 over the head domain label, the key id as u32be, and the archive format major as u16be (the _archive_subkeys pattern, a third domain).
The head chain over parsed entries: HMAC-chained (seq, tag) pairs from a genesis value, so the digest commits to the count, the order, and every entry's tag at once.

Rewrite the head commitment for the archive's current contents under the keyring's current key. Called by archive_append after the entry line is durable; recomputed from the full file, so it also heals a head left behind by a crash and adopts a pre-Pack-H archive on its first Pack H append.

Verify the head commitment against parsed entries, when a head file exists. Absent head file -> a pre-Pack-H archive, nothing to verify (adoption happens on the next append). A present but malformed head, a count mismatch (the tail-truncation signature), or a chain mismatch -> ArchiveHeld. A head whose key is absent from the ring -> ArchiveLocked.
Archive one replaced meaning under label and return the stored entry dict.
Parse every line of the archive file into entry dicts. Any malformed line raises ArchiveHeld: the archive fails as a whole, never partially.

Read the whole archive: a list of (label, payload) pairs in seq order. Every entry's sequence position and tag is verified before anything is returned, and the head commitment (Pack H) is verified whenever a head file exists — a count or chain mismatch raises ArchiveHeld, so a tail truncated at a clean line boundary no longer reads as verified. Any failure raises (ArchiveLocked for an absent key, ArchiveHeld for any verification failure) and NOTHING is returned. A missing archive file reads as an empty list.

Report the archive's state, without raising for content problems: "absent" (no archive file), "verified" (every entry verifies), "held" (any entry fails verification or is malformed), "locked" (the keyring, or a key an entry needs, is absent).

The most recently archived payload under label, or None if the label was never archived. Reads through archive_read_all: a held archive raises ArchiveHeld here too -- a lookup never answers from an unverified archive.
True iff fn() raises exc_type (a different exception, or no exception, is a failure).
Write text to a path as UTF-8.
Run all persistence checks. Return list of (name, value).
Check results against expected values. Return list of (name, passed, actual, want) tuples.
Run suite twice, verify determinism, print results.
Canonical JSON bytes for hashing: sorted keys, tight separators.
SHA-256 over the record fields excluding the hash itself.
Words for the index. If payload has a 'words' list, use it; else extract lowercase alphanumeric tokens from string fields.
Check seqs, links, hashes, and that every record's namespace matches the file it was read from.
Open the pool store in a directory: load every namespace file, note torn files, and build the word indexes.
The JSONL file path for a pool namespace.
Load one pool file's records, treating a torn final line as truncation.
Index one pool record under every word its payload contains.
Raise ValueError for a namespace the pool store does not carry.
Verify one file's chain, or all four. True, or raise ValueError naming the broken file.

Append one record to the namespace's file. Durable (fsync) before returning. graph: optional graph address tuple (layer, dimension, index); when supplied, it is validated with the pmca_graphspace rules and stored in the payload as a JSON-safe 'graph' list [layer, dimension, index]. When omitted, the payload is stored exactly as given.
Record by namespace + seq, or None.
Records of one pool file, in seq order.
Records (across all four pools) whose payload mentions the word. Deterministic order: NAMESPACES order, then seq order within each pool.
One pool's records, or all four concatenated in NAMESPACES order. Deterministic: two replays identical.

Mark a record superseded WITHOUT editing or deleting it (A5). Returns a new record in the same pool pointing back. new_payload: dict (merged into the supersession payload) or string (used as the reason). graph: optional graph address, passed through to append().
Flush, fsync, close all four files. Idempotent.

Append a teaching event's audit entry to the 'audit' namespace. Helper only; the teaching loop itself is NOT modified here. Payload = the audit entry dict (preferred), with a 'words' list extracted from the input text for the word index. graph: optional graph address, passed through to append().
Append an unvalued edge's sandbox evaluation record. graph: optional graph address, passed through to append().

Append one engagement record (a dict payload) to the 'engagement' namespace, and nothing else. Same machinery as sandbox_record: the pool's own append (hash-chained, fsynced). graph: optional graph address, passed through to append().
The pools module's battery assertion helper: record and print PASS or FAIL for a named condition.
The pools module's own test battery.
Content fingerprint of the current LEXICON / EDGE_TABLE bindings.
Materialize this module's seed GraphSpace from the CURRENT table bindings; rebuilt when the bindings' contents change.
Seed entry (POS tag tuple) for a word, via the space, or None.
Harm of the (source, target) edge, read from the graph holding the source entry (or the source's dist_address graph when the source has no entry placement), or None when unmapped.

Derive the topic from entries present in the input (Ruling A). Violence target present (person/him/bomb/...) -> "violence". Else cooking entry present and no violence entry other than the verb itself -> "cooking". Else None (no conditioning, base edge values). Pure lookup over the token tuple; deterministic.

Topic-conditioned edge value (Ruling A, 2026-10-15). When the topic is cooking, (sharp, knife) harm = 0, not 2: a sharp knife in a cooking topic is a kitchen tool, not a hazard. All other edges, and (sharp, knife) under violence / None topic, use the base table value. Applied BEFORE cascade totaling, in build_edges.
Lowercase, strip punctuation, split whitespace. Deterministic.
Words in the input that the proof lexicon does not know.
Deterministic POS tagging by dictionary lookup + grammar rules.

Deterministic parse: tokens, POS, verb/subject/object, adjectives, topic, with-phrase, passive voice. Rulings A / C / E (2026-10-15): topic from entries' relationships; "with X" as instrument or identifier; passive maps to the same edge as active.
Canonical form of a word for proof matching: 'him' maps to 'person'; every other word is itself.

If-then edge selection: language rules + POS pick the edges; harm is read from the selected edges.
