entry.purpose: Apply a remedy's deterministic operations to a world (sandbox or live). Operations are content-level only: fill (set a field), link (append to a list field), derive (copy a stored field's value by rule). Anything else is refused — an unknown operation is a loud failure, never a silent skip.
The union of every token set the analyzer knows: nouns, subject-only words, verbs and their forms, pronouns, articles, possessives, prepositions, conjunctions, marker words and marker tokens.
Lowercase, drop sentence punctuation, single-space.

True iff a foreknowledge marker appears in the token list: a marker word, or a marker phrase as CONSECUTIVE tokens. Pack A: phrase matching is token-boundary — the old substring test armed the gate on "on purposeful" (claims-03 section 5; Argon's find).
True iff a foreknowledge marker appears in the sentence.

Pack A (claims-03 W6): the gate is armed PER CLAUSE. A marker arms the gate only for the clause whose verb it precedes — BEFORE, the ruled axiom's own order. A marker in another clause, or after this clause's verb, does not arm it: before this fix the sentence-global scan fired the child_gate lock on a spine clause because "knowingly" modified a dog's barking in the clause before it. This is clause-scoping hardening of the marker test, NOT the ruled recursive intent loop (a P3-depth build, still open).
The head of a noun-phrase span (Pack A, divergence D2).

The verb position parse_clause selects: the first token whose canonical form is a seed verb; failing that, the first token the dictionary resolved with verb form. None when the clause holds no known verb. Shared by parse_clause and the ST-20 negated-target guard so both always agree on which span is the target span.

Parse one clause. Return (subject, verb, target), or None when the clause holds no known verb. Seed tables win: the verb is the first token found in VERBS, as before; only when no seed verb exists does a dictionary resolution with form "verb" serve (canonical = its headword). Subject and target are the noun-phrase HEADS of their spans (see _np_head); a dictionary head is returned as its token and handled by the caller (it has no seed structure).

True when another verb stands in the clause after the do-form at index i: a later do-form, or a later token the surface attests as verb-capable outside the auxiliary class (a seed verb form, or a dictionary resolution with verb form, when the tier is on). This is the company by which the SENTENCE decides a do-form's class (GRAM-1, RULED 2026-10-28 — his class-by-company doctrine): the form itself carries no class.

The indices of the do-forms standing as their clause's MAIN verb: exactly those with no company after them — "he does his work" (the doing is the action) against "the dog does bite the man" (the bite is; "does" is do-support and contributes nothing).

GRAM-1 frame guard: the one generic/hypothetical shape deterministic from stored structure — a demonstrative subject ("that" / "this") whose do-form has no company, "that does that". The subject is unattested and the clause's only verb material is the auxiliary itself, so no statement geometry exists from which a current state could be read; the frame is generic and the analysis HOLDs naming it, never silently reading the sentence as a current statement. Anything richer (a gerund subject — "doing this does that") has no such signature in stored structure and is beyond this guard's reach by design.

The guard layer's verb oracle: the ONE shared implementation (pmca_verb_capable via pmca_parse_guards.dict_verb_capable, Candidacy Rule Set C-4). RETIRED here (DICT-1 Part 1, WG2 2026-11-01): the seed-table oracle OR that used to extend this wrapper — seed identity is decided by the seed tables' own checks (and, for forms, by _seed_verb_of under Part 2), never by a dictionary oracle (Atlas T-1; C-5).

The seed verb a token IS, under DICT-1 Part 2 (RULED 2026-10-31): the token itself when it is a seed key, the stored form table's target, or — through pmca_forms_resolver, under its armour (per-form attestation, verb-slot sentence-context arbitration) — the seed key whose lemma the token is an attested form of. None when the resolver attests no seed identity (verdict NONE) or HOLDs (ambiguous_form: resolver HOLDs remain HOLDs — no identity is forced here).
The targets of stored part_of edges whose source is the given word, across every graph in the space; empty when the space is None.
A fresh verdict-parameter record with cause, action, target, consequence and directness all None.

inputs.signature: (sentence, verdict, omega, harm, gate, params, edges, trace, hold_reason, lock_reason)

entry.purpose: Assemble the analyzer's result record for a sentence from its verdict, omega, harm, gate, parameters, edges, trace and hold/lock reasons.

The pre-wiring analysis, unchanged except that a coefficient cell missing from the seed tables falls back to the given own space (see _own_coefficient), and, when the dictionary tier is on (see configure_dictionary), a word the seed does not know may resolve through the stored dictionary. Verdicts, harm values, and trace lines are the pre-wiring ones; the additions are one trace note when the own space resolves a cell and one per dictionary resolution. GRAM-1 (2026-10-28) adds the grammar tier's auxiliary jurisdiction inside this flow — the frame guard, the two jurisdiction screens, the unknown-word scan's skip, the main-verb do-forms, and the verb-group negation arm; the blocks are marked GRAM-1 where they stand.
The module's default own space: every analysis made without an explicit space records here, and register_logic writes here. Empty until the first analysis or registration.
Rebind the module's default own space to the given space (the persistence module's load path). Subsequent analyze() and register_logic() calls made without an explicit space use the given space.

First content word of a cleaned sentence: the first token that is a noun, a subject-only word, or a verb (canonical form). With the dictionary tier on, a token in neither the seed tables nor KNOWN that the dictionary resolves also counts (form "other": the token; form "verb": its headword). Falls back to the first token, then to "".

Record one analysis's parameter summary in the own space, at the dist_address home of the sentence's first content word (graph produced on demand, created_by "system"). The record key carries a sequence number from the module record counter, so a later analysis of the same sentence (before and after a registration, say) records alongside the earlier one, never against it. Returns the record's home address.
Coefficient for a (verb, replaceability class) pair from the own space, or None. Only entries written by register_logic count; analysis records never resolve.

Register one piece of own logic: the coefficient for a (verb, replaceability class) pair, keyed "verb:class" (a surface verb form is canonicalized). identifier is the integer coefficient. This API stands in for the gated promotion path: it is the ONLY way logic entries enter the own space, and analyze() never calls it (no self-ratification). Re-registering the same key with the same identifier is a no-op; a different identifier raises GlueConflict, the graphspace glue discipline. Returns the key's home address.

Analyze one sentence. Return the 7 parameters, a verdict, and a trace. closure=True at engagement or document end. With space given, the analysis is recorded in that own space and own logic registered there may resolve seed-missing coefficient cells; with no space, the module's default own space is used.

Point the analyzer at a Webster 1913 DB (see pmca_dictionary.configure). path None turns the tier off. Either way the cached code manifest is dropped: the manifest names the dictionary exactly when one is in use, so a configuration change must recompute it.

True exactly when the dictionary tier can resolve in this process: pmca_dictionary has a DB (configured through configure_dictionary or directly, or PMCA_DICTIONARY_DB is set) and the named file exists. Derived from pmca_dictionary's own state (Pack G, 2026-10-26), so every consultation path — the lexicon scan in _analyze_core, the verb scan, and the parse guards, which consult pmca_dictionary directly — sees the same tier this function reports, and the code manifest, which names the dictionary exactly in this state, agrees with behaviour by construction. (Before Pack G this tracked only the analyzer's own setting while pmca_dictionary silently resolved a default-path DB: the guards consulted a dictionary the manifest omitted — claims audit 06, synthesis D12.)
Canonical JSON: sorted keys, tight separators. The one serialization every hash in this section is computed over.

{module_name: sha256 of file bytes} for the modules whose code determines a verdict, located beside this module. Computed lazily, once per process: determinism is a property of code + state, so the code is pinned by content hash.
SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the analyzer's code manifest.

Point the analyzer's logging surfaces at an atomic entry store. root is a state root (the entry files live under <root>/atomic/, spec 4.1) or an already-open pmca_atomic_entries.EntryStore to share with another surface (a store held by this module is owned and closed on reconfigure; a shared store is left open). root None turns entry writing off: the surfaces return to pool records, exactly as before the pack.

The environment's dictionary block (spec 4.5): ALWAYS present on every entry, from every surface. Off names configured False, db_hash None, source "off" (the ST-71 fix: a dict-off record names its environment instead of naming no dictionary at all). On names the DB hash and how the tier resolved: "explicit" (a configure call), "env" (PMCA_DICTIONARY_DB), or "default" (any other resolution; Pack G removed the default path, so that value is defensive only).

The entry_v 1 environment (spec 4.5): the analyzer's _code_manifest() map and its hash, plus the dictionary block, always named. This is the ONE manifest helper: the other wired surfaces (teaching, write-in) build their entries' environments through it, so every entry in the store names its code and dictionary environment the same way.

The analyzer space serialized EXACTLY as pmca_persistence.save_analyzer_space serializes it (typed encoding, its own checksum): the save runs against a throwaway directory with the keyring state this module's entry store was configured with, and the envelope it writes is read back and embedded in the segment_open entry. The save's own read-back verification runs as part of the save, so a state that could not be loaded back raises here, at segment open, before the segment exists. The generation follows the _checkpoint allocation convention (last recorded + 1), so blob generations stay continuous with the pre-adoption checkpoint generations in the same segment history.
The space to work in: the analyzer's own space when the caller passes None, else the caller's space.
The persistence checksum of a space, used as its fingerprint.

Rebuild segment state by scanning BOTH record sources once: the pool engagement chain (pre-adoption segments) and, when an entry store is configured, the entry store (post-adoption segments; spec 4.4 / build step 3). If the last segment_open in either source has no matching segment_close or segment_discard, that segment is still open. Segment ids are allocated across both sources, so "opens" counts both and ids never repeat across the adoption boundary. state["open_source"] names which source the open segment's records live in ("pool" or "entry"); state["open_checkpoint_entry_seq"] is, for an entry segment, the seq of the segment_open entry carrying its starting state blob. Returns the state dict (also cached per store).
The cached segment state for an entry store, scanning the store's segments on first use.

Save a checkpoint of the effective space when state_root is given; return the generation used, else None. persistence.save_analyzer_space takes (root, space, generation) and returns the file path, so generations are allocated here: the first checkpoint is generation 1, then last recorded + 1 (the demo app's convention; the chain is the record of generations).

Append a segment_open ENTRY embedding the serialized starting state (the blob is the CURRENT space serialization) and swing the segment state to the new segment, in place. The inner half of _engagement_open_entry, split out so the seal path (_seal_analysis_entry) can open the next segment inside its own hold of the entry store's lock when a count close fires there: the caller holds the lock, passes the state, and has already decided a new segment is wanted.

engagement_open on the entry path (atomic-entry pack): append a segment_open ENTRY embedding the serialized starting state, and return the new segment id. If an entry segment is already open, return its id. If a POOL segment is still open (the adoption boundary), close it in the pool chain first, reason "adoption", so exactly one segment is open across both sources and its records live in one of them. state_root / _checkpoint play no part here: the entry carries the state, so there is no way to open a segment without it. One critical section under the pool store's lock, as on the pool path (the entry store's own append takes its lock inside this hold).

Open a segment in the store, or return the open one's id. Appends a segment_open record {segment_id, opening_fingerprint, checkpoint_generation}. When state_root is given, a checkpoint of the effective space is saved first and its generation recorded.

Append a segment_close ENTRY for the open entry segment the passed state describes, carrying the close fields exactly as the pool segment_close payload computes them (segment_id, reason, engagements, first_seq, last_seq, segment_head, closing_fingerprint, and the segment key by the same formula -- computed over ENTRY seqs, with segment_head the seal of the segment's last engagement entry, or "GENESIS" if the segment holds none), then clear the open-segment fields in place. The inner half of _engagement_close_entry, split out for the seal path (see _open_entry_segment): the caller holds the lock and has checked the open segment is entry-backed.

engagement_close on the entry path (atomic-entry pack): append a segment_close ENTRY carrying the close fields exactly as the pool segment_close payload computes them (see _close_entry_segment). Returns the sealed entry, or None when the open segment is not entry-backed, in which case the pool path applies. One critical section under the pool store's lock, as on the pool path.

Close the open segment with a key, or return None if no segment is open. When state_root is given, a checkpoint is saved first and its generation recorded. The key is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of {closing_fingerprint, segment_head, first_seq, last_seq}, where segment_head is the hash of the segment's last engagement record, or "GENESIS" if the segment holds none. Returns the stored close record. One critical section under the store's lock: the key is computed over the segment state and the close record appended atomically with the state transition.

Close the open segment WITHOUT a key, marking it discarded by a record (D5: discards are marked, never vaporized). Returns the stored discard record, or None if no segment is open. One critical section under the store's lock, like engagement_open and engagement_close.

{open_segment, engagements_in_open_segment, closed_segments, discarded_segments, last_key} for a store, from the recovery cache (scanning the chain on first use). Read under the store's lock so the snapshot cannot straddle another thread's segment transition.
Rational pair as a JSON list [num, den]; None stays None. Floats never appear: pairs are integers by construction.

Build the engagement record payload (build spec: Engagement record payload). The single builder shared by analyze_logged and log_result, so both paths record identically. claim_id is left None here and set by _append_engagement, the only caller, from the seq the record is about to receive.

inputs.signature: (store, space, sentence, closure, result, before_checksum, after_checksum)

entry.purpose: Append one engagement record for an already-computed result: ensure a segment is open, build the payload, append, apply the auto-close rule (the append that brings the open segment to 100 engagements closes it, reason "count", immediately after). Returns the stored record. Append exceptions propagate (loud, per design); the result is already computed and is never altered here.

inputs.signature: (handle, store, space, sentence, closure, result, before_checksum, after_checksum, segment_id)

entry.purpose: The one shared entry builder for analysis processes (atomic-entry pack; the _engagement_payload sharing precedent): journal the result's trace entries as steps, in emission order, and seal the entry with outcome = the output object _engagement_payload builds, verbatim.

analyze_logged on the entry path: the analysis runs INSIDE the entry lifecycle (spec 4.4). The entry is begun (input {sentence, closure}, durable) before analyze() runs; an exception from the analysis files the process incomplete immediately and propagates unchanged. The caller is acknowledged only after the entry is durable. Returns (result, sealed_entry).
log_result on the entry path: same lifecycle as _analyze_logged_entry, for a result computed elsewhere. Both fingerprints are taken at call time, as on the pool path. Returns the sealed entry.

analyze() with its engagement recorded. With store None, identical to analyze() and the record is None. Else: ensure a segment is open, fingerprint the effective space before, call analyze(), fingerprint after, append the engagement record, return (result, stored_record). The result is fully computed before any logging, so a logging failure (which propagates, loudly) can never alter it.

Record an engagement for a result computed elsewhere (the app-facing path: the Space's GPU call returns a result, and logging happens on the CPU side from that result, never by re-running analyze()). The before/after fingerprints are both taken at call time; for a pure analysis they are equal under the record filter, which is the design's invariant. Returns the stored record, or None when store is None.
Run all test cases. Return list of result tuples.
Check results against expected values. Return list of (name, passed, actual, want) tuples.
Run suite twice, verify determinism, print results.
Run the graphspace wiring checks. Return list of (name, passed, detail) tuples.
Run wiring checks twice, verify determinism, print.

Build the fixture dictionary in dirpath and return its path. Schema is the production one (defs: word -> JSON list of definition strings). Verb entries carry definitions beginning "To " (the GCIDE infinitive convention); the cat entry's definitions do not.
Run the dictionary wiring checks. Return list of (name, passed, detail) tuples.
Run dictionary checks twice, verify determinism, print.
Secondary recognition via the word's genus (pmca_isa).
Return a copy of the append-only audit log.
Empty the audit log. Test isolation only; production use keeps a single append-only log and never calls this.
Allocate the next teaching event id from the module counter.

Point the teaching surface at an atomic entry store. root is a state root (the entry files live under <root>/atomic/, spec 4.1) or an already-open pmca_atomic_entries.EntryStore to share with another surface (a store held by this module is owned and closed on reconfigure; a shared store is left open). root None turns entry writing off: teach/approve behave exactly as before the pack. Hosts configure once, before teaching.

The entry_v 1 environment for teaching entries: the ONE manifest helper is the analyzer's (spec 4.5), reached by a call-time import, so every surface's entries name their code and dictionary environment the same way.

The steps of a teach process, from the records teach itself made, in the order teach records them: the explanation parse, then the audit entry's findings in the audit entry's own order (applied updates, rejected updates, generalizations proposed / confirmed / flagged, superseded records, verification, regressions, conflicts). A door refusal appends no audit entry; its step is the refusal itself.

The steps of an approve process: the supersession operations in the order approve performs them. A refused approval records the conflict gate's findings (one conflict step per recorded conflict) and the refusal; an approved one records each archived proposal, then the promotion.

Place one taught edge into an own space: its source word's entry goes to the source's dist_address home (graph produced on demand), and the edge rides on that graph -- mirroring how the seed space stores edges on their source word's home graph. The entry and edge objects are shared with the seed's flat views, so a materialized space and the seed can never disagree.

Materialize the POTENTIAL own space of a pending seed: the pending event's candidates -- its applied taught edges (provenance "teaching:<event_id>", including confirmed generalizations of the event, whose provenance extends it) placed as edges on their source words' home graphs, and each pending generalization proposal placed as an entry at its source word's dist_address home. A seed that is not pending materializes an empty space. Deterministic: the same pending seed always materializes a byte-identical space.

Materialize the LIVE own space of a seed: every taught edge (provenance "teaching:<event_id>" of any event) placed on its source word's home graph. For an approved seed this is the system's own logic, live. Deterministic: the same seed always materializes a byte-identical space.
Refresh the module-held potential space from a pending seed. No-op for a seed that is not pending.

Promote a just-approved event's candidates into the held LIVE own space. Approval is cumulative -- the approved seed carries every previously promoted taught edge -- so the live space is rebuilt from the approved seed and holds the system's full live own logic. The event's held potential space is released: its applied candidates are live now, and its unresolved proposals were archived-and-removed by approve() before this runs, so they never enter the live space.
The module-held POTENTIAL own space (the latest pending event's candidates), or None before any teach().
The module-held LIVE own space: the system's own logic as promoted by approve() (an empty space until the first approval).

The own-space graph address of entries taught from the given source word: its dist_address home on Layer 1 -- the address home_of(source) reports in the own spaces. This is the address a caller passes as graph= to pmca_pools.audit_to_pool when writing an audit record about such an entry.
The event counter's current integer value: the N of the most recently minted "teach-N" event id (0 before any teach()).
A copy of the in-memory audit log list.

The LIVE own space to hold after restoring the given seed: live_own_space(seed) when the seed is not pending. For a pending seed, the pending event's candidates are potential, not live -- they are excluded (same provenance predicate potential_own_space uses to select them), so a restore can never present unapproved logic as live. One consequence: an edge the pending event re-stamped (a modification of previously taught logic) drops out of the restored live space until approval; its pre-teach form is not recoverable from the pending seed alone. The restored live space errs toward showing less live logic, never unapproved logic.
Restore the module's primary state from a persisted seed dict, event counter, and audit log (the persistence module's load path).
Canonical form of a word for teaching matching: 'him' maps to 'person'; every other word is itself.

Mirror of pmca_proof.build_edges, reading harm from the given seed table instead of the proof's module-level EDGE_TABLE. Returns None on HOLD or on any unmapped edge (honest closed-world). Idiom and compound edges are read from the seed table too: an unvalued idiom edge in the seed yields HOLD, where the proof's hardcoded table yields APPROVE. The seed is the authority here. Compounds are looked up in pmca_proof.COMPOUNDS (no hard-coded compound); a compound is one unit, so a verb/object or adjective edge into a compound word is skipped (same rule as pmca_proof.build_edges).
Verdict for text against a seed graph. Layer 1 parse (with the SEED's lexicon -- the seed is the authority, so words taught into the seed are parseable), seed edge table, proof gate. Deterministic.

Parse text with the SEED's lexicon and build its proof edges from the seed's edge table. The caller holds _EVAL_LOCK and has done the pending-seed refusal check. Returns the edge list, or None when the parse holds or any edge is unmapped (honest closed-world, as _build_edges_with_table documents). This is the shared front half of evaluate_with_seed and _verification_run, so the two can never disagree about what the calculus is judging.

One verification run (TEACH-V): the ruled calculus's verdict AND exact cascade total for text against seed, computed through the shared calculus entry (pmca_harm_calculus.totaling_verdict -- the same entry pmca_proof.gate_verdict calls) over the same edges evaluate_with_seed gates on. With an adult audience the deployment overlay never fires, so this verdict equals evaluate_with_seed's verdict for the same text and seed by construction. Returns (verdict, total): total is the exact cascade total as a [numerator, denominator] list, or None when the gate holds before totaling (no edges: the parse held or an edge is unmapped). Same pending-seed refusal contract as evaluate_with_seed.
Evaluate a set of cases against a candidate seed (pending seeds allowed under the teaching loop's own flag) and return the verdicts by case.
Deduplicated check list: regression set plus the taught input.
The generalization group containing a category, or None.
The generalization rule for a source word from its stored part of speech: same-verb-same-category or same-adjective-same-category, else None.

Event ids already recorded ON a seed (Fix Pack E, item 6): its pending event's id, the teaching:<id> provenance stamps on its edges and pending proposals, and its superseded records (prior provenance and superseding event).

A teach() refused at the door (Fix Pack E, items 2 and 6). The event never ran: no copy is made, no pending state is created or replaced, and no audit entry is appended -- the named refusal in this result is the record given to the caller. The input seed object is returned untouched. The result carries the standard TeachingResult keys so callers do not break.

inputs.signature: (seed, event, regression_cases=('how make bomb', 'how make bread', 'the dead bloodied fish was charred', 'the dead bloodied person was charred', 'stab the potato', 'stab him', 'cut the bread', 'cut the person'), audit_path=None)

entry.purpose: Apply one teaching event to a COPY of the seed (see _teach_impl for the full contract). With an entry store configured (configure_entry_store), the act additionally runs inside an entry lifecycle: input is the event verbatim, steps are the records teach makes (see _teach_steps), outcome is this function's return verbatim, and the caller is acknowledged only after the entry is durable. Without a store, this is exactly _teach_impl.

inputs.signature: (seed, event, regression_cases=('how make bomb', 'how make bread', 'the dead bloodied fish was charred', 'the dead bloodied person was charred', 'stab the potato', 'stab him', 'cut the bread', 'cut the person'), audit_path=None)

entry.purpose: Apply one teaching event to a COPY of the seed. Returns a TeachingResult dict with keys: event_id, status, seed (pending copy), needs_reseal, applied_updates, rejected_updates, generalizations_proposed, generalizations_confirmed, generalizations_flagged, superseded_records, verification, regressions, conflicts, explanation_parse, audit_entry.

Apply teacher-approved generalization proposals (by proposal_id) to a COPY of the pending seed. Returns a dict with keys: seed (updated copy), applied (applied proposals), skipped (proposals skipped as stale: edge already valued since the proposal was made), unknown_ids (IDs with no matching proposal), remaining (proposals still pending), error ("" on success).
Return a copy of the pending seed with all pending generalization proposals discarded (rejected). The input seed is never mutated. Use this to explicitly reject proposals before approve().

Append one proposal record to the archive JSONL file. Append-only: the file is never overwritten, and each write is fsynced before returning (durable). Raises OSError on write failure; the caller treats that as an approval failure so no proposal is ever lost.

Read the proposals archive JSONL file and return the archived proposals (in order). If the file does not exist, return []. If any non-empty line is not valid JSON, raise ValueError — a corrupted archive is reported, never silently skipped.
Return the archived proposal record with the given proposal_id, or None if no such record exists.

Promote PENDING -> CURRENT (see _approve_impl for the full contract). With an entry store configured (configure_entry_store), the act additionally runs inside an entry lifecycle: input is the pending-event reference, steps are the supersession operations in order (see _approve_steps), outcome is this function's return verbatim, and the caller is acknowledged only after the entry is durable. Without a store, this is exactly _approve_impl.

Promote PENDING -> CURRENT (superposition model). Re-verifies the pending seed: the taught case must still yield the pending event's VERIFICATION verdict (TEACH-V: the verdict of record teach() computed and replay-confirmed; the recorded human verdict is provenance and is never compared here), no held verification outcome may promote, and every regression case must still yield its recorded post-teaching verdict (detects tampering with the pending seed after teach()).
AST check: no call to maximum anywhere in this file.
AST check: no float literal anywhere in this file.
AST check: no random import anywhere in this file.
Grep check: the forbidden guessing verb does not appear in this file. Pattern is built from parts so the checker does not match itself.
The teaching module's own test battery.
A definition with its leading GCIDE apparatus stripped: "(...)" field labels and "(a)" sense markers are apparatus, not sense text.
True iff this stored definition is a verb sense under the cleaned Webster-convention decoding: its cleaned text begins "To ".
(has_verb_senses, has_nonverb_senses) over stored definitions, by the cleaned decoding.
"verb" iff any definition is a verb sense under the cleaned decoding, else "other". This is the value pmca_dictionary.lookup reports as "form"; its tier is CANDIDATE (see pos_answer), never attested.
One attestation record in the shared shape. `field` names the field the evidence is FOR; class counting is per-field (classes_for_field), so evidence recorded for one field can never promote another.

The distinct provenance CLASSES over attestation records of exactly `field`, read through the governed source->lineage table (C-3). Records of any other field contribute nothing — POS evidence never counts for genus and genus evidence never counts for POS.

DICT-1 Part 3 (RULED 2026-10-31 BY ALDER UNDER DELEGATION): the sealed lineage-independence measurement for POS/forms is permitted — and on current stores expected — to BE the negative result. No witness with real cross-lineage coverage exists in today's stores (POS cross-lineage overlap n=3 in the verification store; ECDICT POS unmeasurable in principle; OEWN forms never recorded), so the mechanism answers UNMEASURED for POS and forms, and the honest answer for any other field it has no measurement for. It never invents a measured value.
C-6: while POS/forms lineage independence is UNMEASURED, lineage-counted promotion in POS/forms is disabled. True for POS and forms on today's stores.

The C-1 candidacy answer for one word's POS capability: {"word", "tier", "value", "provenance_classes", "attestations", "gap"} where value is {"verb_capable": bool, "noun_capable": bool} at CANDIDATE tier, or None at UNKNOWN tier (no dictionary entry — the gap record names why). Tier "attested" is never returned by this mechanism for POS: structural POS governs where attested by any lineage (none is wired here), the cleaned decoding is CANDIDATE only (C-4), and lineage-counted promotion is blocked while independence is UNMEASURED (C-6).
Boolean projection of pos_answer: the word carries a verb candidate (attested or CANDIDATE tier). This is the one verb_capable every consumer in the tree calls.
Boolean projection of pos_answer: the word carries a noun candidate (a sense that is not a verb-form sense).
The distinct attested values of one field, in first-attestation order, by canonical JSON identity.

Gate one dossier into its home entry in `store` (a pmca_write_in store — the one permanent storage shape). Returns {"word", "outcome", "fields": {field: {"disposition": "crossed"|"held_conflicted"| "held_unattested", ...}}}. "outcome" is "built" when every dossier field crossed, "built_with_gaps" when at least one field was held at the gate (its gap recorded), "held" when no field crossed.
The union of every token set the analyzer knows: nouns, subject-only words, verbs and their forms, pronouns, articles, possessives, prepositions, conjunctions, marker words and marker tokens.
Lowercase, drop sentence punctuation, single-space.

True iff a foreknowledge marker appears in the token list: a marker word, or a marker phrase as CONSECUTIVE tokens. Pack A: phrase matching is token-boundary — the old substring test armed the gate on "on purposeful" (claims-03 section 5; Argon's find).
True iff a foreknowledge marker appears in the sentence.

Pack A (claims-03 W6): the gate is armed PER CLAUSE. A marker arms the gate only for the clause whose verb it precedes — BEFORE, the ruled axiom's own order. A marker in another clause, or after this clause's verb, does not arm it: before this fix the sentence-global scan fired the child_gate lock on a spine clause because "knowingly" modified a dog's barking in the clause before it. This is clause-scoping hardening of the marker test, NOT the ruled recursive intent loop (a P3-depth build, still open).
The head of a noun-phrase span (Pack A, divergence D2).

The verb position parse_clause selects: the first token whose canonical form is a seed verb; failing that, the first token the dictionary resolved with verb form. None when the clause holds no known verb. Shared by parse_clause and the ST-20 negated-target guard so both always agree on which span is the target span.

Parse one clause. Return (subject, verb, target), or None when the clause holds no known verb. Seed tables win: the verb is the first token found in VERBS, as before; only when no seed verb exists does a dictionary resolution with form "verb" serve (canonical = its headword). Subject and target are the noun-phrase HEADS of their spans (see _np_head); a dictionary head is returned as its token and handled by the caller (it has no seed structure).

True when another verb stands in the clause after the do-form at index i: a later do-form, or a later token the surface attests as verb-capable outside the auxiliary class (a seed verb form, or a dictionary resolution with verb form, when the tier is on). This is the company by which the SENTENCE decides a do-form's class (GRAM-1, RULED 2026-10-28 — his class-by-company doctrine): the form itself carries no class.

The indices of the do-forms standing as their clause's MAIN verb: exactly those with no company after them — "he does his work" (the doing is the action) against "the dog does bite the man" (the bite is; "does" is do-support and contributes nothing).

GRAM-1 frame guard: the one generic/hypothetical shape deterministic from stored structure — a demonstrative subject ("that" / "this") whose do-form has no company, "that does that". The subject is unattested and the clause's only verb material is the auxiliary itself, so no statement geometry exists from which a current state could be read; the frame is generic and the analysis HOLDs naming it, never silently reading the sentence as a current statement. Anything richer (a gerund subject — "doing this does that") has no such signature in stored structure and is beyond this guard's reach by design.

The guard layer's verb oracle: the ONE shared implementation (pmca_verb_capable via pmca_parse_guards.dict_verb_capable, Candidacy Rule Set C-4). RETIRED here (DICT-1 Part 1, WG2 2026-11-01): the seed-table oracle OR that used to extend this wrapper — seed identity is decided by the seed tables' own checks (and, for forms, by _seed_verb_of under Part 2), never by a dictionary oracle (Atlas T-1; C-5).

The dictionary-configuration fingerprint the lemma map is a function of (WG2c F-A fix, 2026-11-01): the resolved DB path plus its content hash (pmca_dictionary.file_hash, itself cached per path), or (None, None) when the tier is off. The resolver's lemma derivation reads the dictionary through _exact_headword, so the map is dictionary- dependent; keying the cache on this fingerprint makes the cached map a pure function of (seed tables, dictionary configuration) — any configuration change, through configure_dictionary OR directly through pmca_dictionary.configure / the environment, yields a different key and a rebuilt map.

The seed lemma map for the CURRENT dictionary configuration, built lazily and cached under its fingerprint (see _dictionary_fingerprint). Before the WG2c fix the first-built map was cached for the process lifetime: an analyze() before configure_dictionary() poisoned the map (the OFF map is the identity map), the ruled DICT-1 Part 2 crush lock then silently HOLDed for the rest of the process, and no gap was recorded.

The seed verb a token IS, under DICT-1 Part 2 (RULED 2026-10-31): the token itself when it is a seed key, the stored form table's target, or — through pmca_forms_resolver, under its armour (per-form attestation, verb-slot sentence-context arbitration) — the seed key whose lemma the token is an attested form of. None when the resolver attests no seed identity (verdict NONE) or HOLDs (ambiguous_form: resolver HOLDs remain HOLDs — no identity is forced here).
The targets of stored part_of edges whose source is the given word, across every graph in the space; empty when the space is None.
A fresh verdict-parameter record with cause, action, target, consequence and directness all None.

inputs.signature: (sentence, verdict, omega, harm, gate, params, edges, trace, hold_reason, lock_reason)

entry.purpose: Assemble the analyzer's result record for a sentence from its verdict, omega, harm, gate, parameters, edges, trace and hold/lock reasons.

The pre-wiring analysis, unchanged except that a coefficient cell missing from the seed tables falls back to the given own space (see _own_coefficient), and, when the dictionary tier is on (see configure_dictionary), a word the seed does not know may resolve through the stored dictionary. Verdicts, harm values, and trace lines are the pre-wiring ones; the additions are one trace note when the own space resolves a cell and one per dictionary resolution. GRAM-1 (2026-10-28) adds the grammar tier's auxiliary jurisdiction inside this flow — the frame guard, the two jurisdiction screens, the unknown-word scan's skip, the main-verb do-forms, and the verb-group negation arm; the blocks are marked GRAM-1 where they stand.
The module's default own space: every analysis made without an explicit space records here, and register_logic writes here. Empty until the first analysis or registration.
Rebind the module's default own space to the given space (the persistence module's load path). Subsequent analyze() and register_logic() calls made without an explicit space use the given space.

First content word of a cleaned sentence: the first token that is a noun, a subject-only word, or a verb (canonical form). With the dictionary tier on, a token in neither the seed tables nor KNOWN that the dictionary resolves also counts (form "other": the token; form "verb": its headword). Falls back to the first token, then to "".

Record one analysis's parameter summary in the own space, at the dist_address home of the sentence's first content word (graph produced on demand, created_by "system"). The record key carries a sequence number from the module record counter, so a later analysis of the same sentence (before and after a registration, say) records alongside the earlier one, never against it. Returns the record's home address.
Coefficient for a (verb, replaceability class) pair from the own space, or None. Only entries written by register_logic count; analysis records never resolve.

Register one piece of own logic: the coefficient for a (verb, replaceability class) pair, keyed "verb:class" (a surface verb form is canonicalized). identifier is the integer coefficient. This API stands in for the gated promotion path: it is the ONLY way logic entries enter the own space, and analyze() never calls it (no self-ratification). Re-registering the same key with the same identifier is a no-op; a different identifier raises GlueConflict, the graphspace glue discipline. Returns the key's home address.

Analyze one sentence. Return the 7 parameters, a verdict, and a trace. closure=True at engagement or document end. With space given, the analysis is recorded in that own space and own logic registered there may resolve seed-missing coefficient cells; with no space, the module's default own space is used.

Point the analyzer at a Webster 1913 DB (see pmca_dictionary.configure). path None turns the tier off. Either way the cached code manifest is dropped: the manifest names the dictionary exactly when one is in use, so a configuration change must recompute it. The cached lemma map is likewise dropped (WG2c F-A fix): it is dictionary-dependent, so a configuration change invalidates it here, and _lemma_map's fingerprint key rebuilds it under the new configuration on next use (the key also covers configuration routes that bypass this function).

True exactly when the dictionary tier can resolve in this process: pmca_dictionary has a DB (configured through configure_dictionary or directly, or PMCA_DICTIONARY_DB is set) and the named file exists. Derived from pmca_dictionary's own state (Pack G, 2026-10-26), so every consultation path — the lexicon scan in _analyze_core, the verb scan, and the parse guards, which consult pmca_dictionary directly — sees the same tier this function reports, and the code manifest, which names the dictionary exactly in this state, agrees with behaviour by construction. (Before Pack G this tracked only the analyzer's own setting while pmca_dictionary silently resolved a default-path DB: the guards consulted a dictionary the manifest omitted — claims audit 06, synthesis D12.)
Canonical JSON: sorted keys, tight separators. The one serialization every hash in this section is computed over.

{module_name: sha256 of file bytes} for the modules whose code determines a verdict, located beside this module. Computed lazily, once per process: determinism is a property of code + state, so the code is pinned by content hash.
SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the analyzer's code manifest.

Point the analyzer's logging surfaces at an atomic entry store. root is a state root (the entry files live under <root>/atomic/, spec 4.1) or an already-open pmca_atomic_entries.EntryStore to share with another surface (a store held by this module is owned and closed on reconfigure; a shared store is left open). root None turns entry writing off: the surfaces return to pool records, exactly as before the pack.

The environment's dictionary block (spec 4.5): ALWAYS present on every entry, from every surface. Off names configured False, db_hash None, source "off" (the ST-71 fix: a dict-off record names its environment instead of naming no dictionary at all). On names the DB hash and how the tier resolved: "explicit" (a configure call), "env" (PMCA_DICTIONARY_DB), or "default" (any other resolution; Pack G removed the default path, so that value is defensive only).

The entry_v 1 environment (spec 4.5): the analyzer's _code_manifest() map and its hash, plus the dictionary block, always named. This is the ONE manifest helper: the other wired surfaces (teaching, write-in) build their entries' environments through it, so every entry in the store names its code and dictionary environment the same way.

The analyzer space serialized EXACTLY as pmca_persistence.save_analyzer_space serializes it (typed encoding, its own checksum): the save runs against a throwaway directory with the keyring state this module's entry store was configured with, and the envelope it writes is read back and embedded in the segment_open entry. The save's own read-back verification runs as part of the save, so a state that could not be loaded back raises here, at segment open, before the segment exists. The generation follows the _checkpoint allocation convention (last recorded + 1), so blob generations stay continuous with the pre-adoption checkpoint generations in the same segment history.
The space to work in: the analyzer's own space when the caller passes None, else the caller's space.
The persistence checksum of a space, used as its fingerprint.

Rebuild segment state by scanning BOTH record sources once: the pool engagement chain (pre-adoption segments) and, when an entry store is configured, the entry store (post-adoption segments; spec 4.4 / build step 3). If the last segment_open in either source has no matching segment_close or segment_discard, that segment is still open. Segment ids are allocated across both sources, so "opens" counts both and ids never repeat across the adoption boundary. state["open_source"] names which source the open segment's records live in ("pool" or "entry"); state["open_checkpoint_entry_seq"] is, for an entry segment, the seq of the segment_open entry carrying its starting state blob. Returns the state dict (also cached per store).
The cached segment state for an entry store, scanning the store's segments on first use.

Save a checkpoint of the effective space when state_root is given; return the generation used, else None. persistence.save_analyzer_space takes (root, space, generation) and returns the file path, so generations are allocated here: the first checkpoint is generation 1, then last recorded + 1 (the demo app's convention; the chain is the record of generations).

Append a segment_open ENTRY embedding the serialized starting state (the blob is the CURRENT space serialization) and swing the segment state to the new segment, in place. The inner half of _engagement_open_entry, split out so the seal path (_seal_analysis_entry) can open the next segment inside its own hold of the entry store's lock when a count close fires there: the caller holds the lock, passes the state, and has already decided a new segment is wanted.

engagement_open on the entry path (atomic-entry pack): append a segment_open ENTRY embedding the serialized starting state, and return the new segment id. If an entry segment is already open, return its id. If a POOL segment is still open (the adoption boundary), close it in the pool chain first, reason "adoption", so exactly one segment is open across both sources and its records live in one of them. state_root / _checkpoint play no part here: the entry carries the state, so there is no way to open a segment without it. One critical section under the pool store's lock, as on the pool path (the entry store's own append takes its lock inside this hold).

Open a segment in the store, or return the open one's id. Appends a segment_open record {segment_id, opening_fingerprint, checkpoint_generation}. When state_root is given, a checkpoint of the effective space is saved first and its generation recorded.

Append a segment_close ENTRY for the open entry segment the passed state describes, carrying the close fields exactly as the pool segment_close payload computes them (segment_id, reason, engagements, first_seq, last_seq, segment_head, closing_fingerprint, and the segment key by the same formula -- computed over ENTRY seqs, with segment_head the seal of the segment's last engagement entry, or "GENESIS" if the segment holds none), then clear the open-segment fields in place. The inner half of _engagement_close_entry, split out for the seal path (see _open_entry_segment): the caller holds the lock and has checked the open segment is entry-backed.

engagement_close on the entry path (atomic-entry pack): append a segment_close ENTRY carrying the close fields exactly as the pool segment_close payload computes them (see _close_entry_segment). Returns the sealed entry, or None when the open segment is not entry-backed, in which case the pool path applies. One critical section under the pool store's lock, as on the pool path.

Close the open segment with a key, or return None if no segment is open. When state_root is given, a checkpoint is saved first and its generation recorded. The key is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of {closing_fingerprint, segment_head, first_seq, last_seq}, where segment_head is the hash of the segment's last engagement record, or "GENESIS" if the segment holds none. Returns the stored close record. One critical section under the store's lock: the key is computed over the segment state and the close record appended atomically with the state transition.

Close the open segment WITHOUT a key, marking it discarded by a record (D5: discards are marked, never vaporized). Returns the stored discard record, or None if no segment is open. One critical section under the store's lock, like engagement_open and engagement_close.

{open_segment, engagements_in_open_segment, closed_segments, discarded_segments, last_key} for a store, from the recovery cache (scanning the chain on first use). Read under the store's lock so the snapshot cannot straddle another thread's segment transition.
